speaker: Unknown
en: Hi, I'm John and I'm a partner at YC.
zh: 嗨，我是 John，我是 YC 的一位合伙人。

speaker: Unknown
en: I often meet founders who have lots of ideas about what to work on and can't decide between them.
zh: 我经常遇到有很多关于做什么事情的想法的创始人，他们无法在这些想法之间做出决定。

speaker: Unknown
en: Sometimes they're working on multiple things.
zh: 有时候他们在同时做好几件事。

speaker: Unknown
en: Often they'll say that they're waiting to find the best idea before fully committing.
zh: 通常他们会说，他们在等到找到最好的想法之后再完全投入。

speaker: Unknown
en: But it's extremely hard to make meaningful progress on a startup without committing to a single idea.
zh: 但是，如果不致力于一个单一的想法，在创业公司上取得有意义的进展是极其困难的。

speaker: Unknown
en: So in this video, I'm going to give you a rubric for how to stop overthinking, pick an idea, commit to it, and then figure out fast whether it's actually working.
zh: 所以在这个视频里，我将给你们一个关于如何停止过度思考、选择一个想法、致力于它，然后快速弄清楚它是否真的在起作用的准则。

speaker: Unknown
en: The most important piece of advice I'd give to founders struggling to pick a startup idea is
zh: 我会给那些在挑选创业公司想法上挣扎的创始人的最重要的建议是

speaker: Unknown
en: Don't overthink it.
zh: 不要过度思考。

speaker: Unknown
en: Overthinking a startup in the earliest days can take many forms, but here are a couple of the most common failure modes I see.
zh: 在最早的日子里过度思考创业公司会有很多种表现形式，但这里是我看到的几种最常见的失败模式。

speaker: Unknown
en: The first is thinking that you need to find the perfect idea.
zh: 第一种是认为你需要找到完美的想法。

speaker: Unknown
en: In some ways, this is an understandable impulse.
zh: 在某些方面，这是一个可以理解的冲动。

speaker: Unknown
en: Startups are hard, so shouldn't you figure out the best idea before committing?
zh: 创业公司很难，所以你不应该在投入之前先弄清楚最好的想法吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: The problem with this approach is that it's impossible to figure out the perfect idea in the abstract.
zh: 这种方法的问题在于，在抽象层面弄清楚完美的想法是不可能的。

speaker: Unknown
en: You can only figure out what you should be working on by making contact with reality and getting feedback from customers.
zh: 你只能通过接触现实并从客户那里获得反馈来弄清楚你应该做什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: The second overthink is, am I the perfect founder for this?
zh: 第二种过度思考是，我是做这个的完美创始人吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: It's true that founder market fit matters.
zh: 创始人市场匹配度确实很重要。

speaker: Unknown
en: A non-technical founder likely won't be the right person to come up with a killer DevTools startup idea, for example.
zh: 例如，一个非技术创始人很可能不是想出一个杀手级的开发者工具创业公司想法的合适人选。

speaker: Unknown
en: But often founders, especially second-time founders, weaponize this line against themselves.
zh: 但往往创始人，尤其是第二次创业的创始人，会把这一论点武器化来针对自己。

speaker: Unknown
en: They convince themselves that they need a decade of domain experience before they can start.
zh: 他们说服自己，他们需要十年的领域经验才能开始。

speaker: Unknown
en: The truth is you don't.
zh: 事实是你不需要。

speaker: Unknown
en: If you pick an idea you're curious about, go extremely deep,
zh: 如果你选了一个你好奇的想法，极其深入地钻研，

speaker: Unknown
en: And most importantly, talk to customers.
zh: 并且最重要的是，与客户交谈。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's often possible to develop extraordinary knowledge in a short amount of time.
zh: 在很短的时间内发展出非凡的知识通常是可能的。

speaker: Unknown
en: We see incredible examples of this all the time at YC.
zh: 我们在 YC 总是看到令人难以置信的例子。

speaker: Unknown
en: Take Blake Scholl, the CEO of Boom Supersonic.
zh: 以 Boom Supersonic 的 CEO Blake Scholl 为例。

speaker: Unknown
en: Blake spent his early career working on ad tech at companies like Amazon and Groupon before deciding to work on commercializing supersonic flight.
zh: Blake 在决定致力于将超音速飞行商业化之前，早期的职业生涯是在 Amazon 和 Groupon 这样的公司从事广告技术工作。

speaker: Unknown
en: Lots of people probably thought he was crazy.
zh: 很多人可能觉得他疯了。

speaker: Unknown
en: But now, Boom is a billion-dollar company.
zh: 但现在，Boom 是一家价值十亿美元的公司。

speaker: Unknown
en: So don't let the question of whether you're allowed to work on something stop you from starting.
zh: 所以不要让“你是否被允许从事这个”这个问题阻止你开始。

speaker: Unknown
en: Once you've stopped overthinking your ideas, it's important to commit to just one.
zh: 一旦你停止过度思考你的想法，致力于其中唯一的一个就很重要了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Often, I meet founders who are working on multiple ideas at once because they believe that this is the best way to figure out which one will actually work.
zh: 我经常遇到同时在做多个想法的创始人，因为他们认为这是弄清楚哪一个真正奏效的最佳方式。

speaker: Unknown
en: There are a couple of problems with this approach.
zh: 这种方法有几个问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: The most serious is that it tends to produce bad data.
zh: 最严重的是它倾向于产生坏数据。

speaker: Unknown
en: If you don't actually go deep on an idea but instead juggle it with several others you won't get good signal about whether what you're doing actually works.
zh: 如果你没有真正深入钻研一个想法，而是同时兼顾其他几个想法，你就无法获得关于你所做的事情是否真的奏效的良好信号。

speaker: Unknown
en: And if you don't get good signal then you could either prematurely talk yourself out of a good idea or convince yourself that a bad one is worth continuing.
zh: 而且如果你没有得到良好的信号，你可能会过早地把自己从一个好的想法中劝退，或者说服自己一个坏的想法值得继续。

speaker: Unknown
en: The solution to this
zh: 对此的解决方案是

speaker: Unknown
en: If you're trying to decide between several ideas, all of which look equally attractive, pick one idea and go deep on it.
zh: 如果你试图在几个看起来同样有吸引力的想法之间做决定，选一个想法并深入钻研它。

speaker: Unknown
en: What do I mean by going deep?
zh: 我所说的深入钻研是什么意思？

speaker: Unknown
en: The first thing is that you should burn the other boats.
zh: 第一件事是你应该烧掉其他的船。

speaker: Unknown
en: That is, you should explicitly foreclose your other startup idea options.
zh: 也就是说，你应该明确地排除你其他的创业公司想法选项。

speaker: Unknown
en: Stop working on them.
zh: 停止做它们。

speaker: Unknown
en: Tell any customers that you've pivoted and work with single-minded focus on the idea you've chosen.
zh: 告诉你所有的客户你已经转型了，并全神贯注地致力于你选择的那个想法。

speaker: Unknown
en: One way to think about going deep is that it should feel like wearing a new skin.
zh: 思考深入的一种方式是，它应该感觉像是穿上了一层新的皮肤。

speaker: Unknown
en: You should become an almost unrecognizable version of yourself.
zh: 你应该成为一个几乎认不出来的版本的自己。

speaker: Unknown
en: This could mean changing your company's name, your emails, your website, and even your internal narrative about why you're building a startup in the first place.
zh: 这可能意味着改变你公司的名字、你的邮箱、你的网站，甚至你关于为什么要建立创业公司的内部叙事。

speaker: Unknown
en: For example, I worked with a startup called GovDash that helps customers win government contracts.
zh: 例如，我与一家名为 GovDash 的创业公司合作过，它帮助客户赢得政府合同。

speaker: Unknown
en: They pivoted at least five times before finding this idea.
zh: 在找到这个想法之前，他们至少转型了五次。

speaker: Unknown
en: And each time they explored something new, they changed their company name and how they talked about their mission.
zh: 每次他们探索新事物时，他们都会改变公司名称和谈论使命的方式。

speaker: Unknown
en: At one point, I forgot how to get in touch with them because they changed their email addresses with each pivot.
zh: 有一次，我都忘了怎么联系他们了，因为他们每次转型都会更改邮箱地址。

speaker: Unknown
en: By truly becoming domain experts in government procurement, their fifth idea worked so well that they could barely keep up with demand.
zh: 通过真正成为政府采购领域的专家，他们的第五个想法效果如此之好，以至于他们几乎无法跟上需求。

speaker: Unknown
en: They recently raised the Series B to scale the business and meet that demand.
zh: 他们最近筹集了 B 轮融资以扩展业务并满足那需求。

speaker: Unknown
en: Once you've decided to fully commit to an idea and go deep, how do you know if you're actually doing it well?
zh: 一旦你决定全身心投入一个想法并深入其中，你如何知道你实际上做得好不好？

speaker: Unknown
en: The high watermark I use to help founders answer this question is could you actually run your customer's business?
zh: 我用来帮助创始人回答这个问题的最高标准是你实际上能经营你客户的业务吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Say you want to build voice customer service agents for cleaning services.
zh: 假设你想为清洁服务构建语音客服智能体。

speaker: Unknown
en: The question isn't just whether you've talked to 20 owners.
zh: 问题不仅仅是你是否和 20 位老板谈过。

speaker: Unknown
en: The question is if I dropped you into a cleaning business tomorrow, would you know how to run it?
zh: 问题是如果我明天把你扔进一家清洁企业，你知道如何经营它吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Do you know what their daily crises are?
zh: 你知道他们日常的危机是什么吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Do you know whether answering the phone is a top five problem?
zh: 你知道接电话是否是前五大问题之一吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Do you know how much business they lose when a call goes unanswered and what they would actually pay to never lose another one?
zh: 你知道当电话未接时他们损失多少业务，以及他们实际上愿意支付多少来不再损失一单吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: These are the kinds of questions you need to be able to answer with very high confidence.
zh: 这些是你需要能够非常有信心地回答的那类问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: Another way to think about this is could you teach a class on the problem you're solving?
zh: 另一种思考方式是，你能就你正在解决的问题开设一门课程吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Are you one of the most informed people in the world on the subject?
zh: 你是这个世界上在这个主题上最了解情况的人之一吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Getting to this level will involve lots of conversations with customers and sometimes even literally doing the job yourself.
zh: 达到这个水平将涉及与客户进行大量对话，有时甚至要亲自去做这项工作。

speaker: Unknown
en: But don't obsess over needing to talk to hundreds of customers before writing code.
zh: 但不要在写代码之前痴迷于需要和数百位客户交谈。

speaker: Unknown
en: The goal is to do both at the same time in a tight loop.
zh: 目标是在一个紧密的循环中同时做这两件事。

speaker: Unknown
en: Deep understanding of customer needs, then product delivery, then deeper understanding of customer needs.
zh: 深入了解客户需求，然后交付产品，然后更深入地了解客户需求。

speaker: Unknown
en: Thank you for watching.
zh: 感谢观看。

speaker: Unknown
en: The most obvious one is pull from customers, but there are several other qualities of good ideas in the AI era that you should look out for as you go.
zh: 最明显的一个是来自客户的拉动，但在 AI 时代，好想法还有其他几个品质，你在进行时应该留意。

speaker: Unknown
en: The first is that the idea sits at the edge of what models can do today.
zh: 第一个是这个想法处于模型今天能做的事情的边缘。

speaker: Unknown
en: This might mean that your product barely works on today's frontier models, but will clearly improve as they get better.
zh: 这可能意味着你的产品在目前的前沿模型上勉强能工作，但会随着它们变好而明显改善。

speaker: Unknown
en: You should understand the bottlenecks impeding your product's performance.
zh: 你应该了解阻碍你产品性能的瓶颈。

speaker: Unknown
en: Intimately, if a particular bottleneck doesn't clear the way you hoped, solving that might become the company.
zh: 密切地，如果某个特定的瓶颈没有像你希望的那样消除，解决它可能就成为了公司。

speaker: Unknown
en: This is a version of Paul Graham's well-known quote that you should live in the future and then build what's missing.
zh: 这是保罗·格雷厄姆著名名言的一个版本，说你应该生活在未来，然后构建缺失的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: The second quality of a good idea is that it should verticalize.
zh: 好想法的第二个品质是它应该垂直化。

speaker: Unknown
en: By this, I mean that it should ultimately sell an outcome.
zh: 我的意思是，它最终应该出售一个结果。

speaker: Unknown
en: For example, providing insurance or medical care rather than just software.
zh: 例如，提供保险或医疗保健，而不仅仅是软件。

speaker: Unknown
en: In the AI era, the cost of producing software is going to zero.
zh: 在 AI 时代，生产软件的成本正在趋近于零。

speaker: Unknown
en: So the things that actually become valuable aren't just software for X.
zh: 所以真正变得有价值的东西不仅仅是 X 的软件。

speaker: Unknown
en: They're customer trust,
zh: 它们是客户信任，

speaker: Unknown
en: Licenses, regulatory permission, and outcome ownership.
zh: 许可证、监管许可和结果所有权。

speaker: Unknown
en: So if you want to get into the insurance space, don't build software for insurance companies.
zh: 所以如果你想进入保险领域，不要为保险公司构建软件。

speaker: Unknown
en: Just be the insurer.
zh: 就成为保险商。

speaker: Unknown
en: Similarly, rather than selling back office software for banks, just be the bank.
zh: 同样，与其为银行销售后台软件，不如成为银行。

speaker: Unknown
en: One example of this is Corgi Insurance, an AI-powered commercial insurance company from YC's Summer 24 batch.
zh: Corgi Insurance 就是一个例子，一家来自 YC 24 年夏季批次的 AI 驱动的商业保险公司。

speaker: Unknown
en: Thank you for watching!
zh: 感谢观看！

speaker: Unknown
en: That brings me to the third quality of a good idea.
zh: 这引出了好想法的第三个品质。

speaker: Unknown
en: It should be the most ambitious version of itself.
zh: 它应该是它自己最雄心勃勃的版本。

speaker: Unknown
en: It may seem unintuitive, but the cost of pursuing a wildly ambitious startup idea and the cost of pursuing a modest one are roughly the same.
zh: 这可能看起来不直观，但追求一个极其雄心勃勃的创业想法的成本和追求一个温和的想法的成本大致相同。

speaker: Unknown
en: They're both extremely hard.
zh: 它们都极其困难。

speaker: Unknown
en: They both place extreme demands on your time.
zh: 它们都对你的时间提出极端的要求。

speaker: Unknown
en: So aim at the version that, if it works, rewrites a sector of the economy.
zh: 所以瞄准那个如果成功，将重写经济部门的版本。

speaker: Unknown
en: Because that's also the version that protects you from competitors, attracts the best talent,
zh: 因为那也是能保护你免受竞争对手伤害、吸引最优秀人才的版本，

speaker: Unknown
en: This could mean building and selling into the most regulated industries like legal, healthcare, or financial services.
zh: 这可能意味着构建并销售给受监管最严格的行业，如法律、医疗保健或金融服务。

speaker: Unknown
en: Or taking on very large incumbents like a $10 billion legacy SaaS company.
zh: 或者挑战非常大的现有企业，比如一家价值 100 亿美元的遗留 SaaS 公司。

speaker: Unknown
en: Or building hard tech like robotics for space assembly.
zh: 或者构建硬科技，比如用于太空组装的机器人技术。

speaker: Unknown
en: Now, what if you do all of this and the idea fails?
zh: 现在，如果你做了所有这些但想法失败了怎么办？

speaker: Unknown
en: The good news is...
zh: 好消息是……

speaker: Unknown
en: You'll be in a dramatically better position than where you started.
zh: 你的处境将比你开始时好得多。

speaker: Unknown
en: And a better sense of how to execute going forward.
zh: 并且对如何继续执行有更好的感觉。

speaker: Unknown
en: But more importantly, you will often come away from the process with a new idea that will actually work.
zh: 但更重要的是，你通常会在这个过程中带着一个真正可行的新想法离开。

speaker: Unknown
en: When most founders begin, they're solving surface-level pain points.
zh: 当大多数创始人开始时，他们正在解决表层痛点。

speaker: Unknown
en: The real opportunities are almost always the deeper structural problems.
zh: 真正的机会几乎总是更深层的结构性问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: In other words, going deep isn't primarily a process for validating the idea you started with.
zh: 换句话说，深入主要不是一个验证你起始想法的过程。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's a way to find the better idea underneath.
zh: 这是一种发现底下那个更好想法的方法。

speaker: Unknown
en: This almost always happens, especially if you're at the forefront of what models can do today.
zh: 这几乎总会发生，特别是如果你处在模型今天能做的事情的最前沿。

speaker: Unknown
en: You'll notice the bottlenecks, the gaps, the dev tools nobody's built, and one of those could turn out to be the actual company.
zh: 你会注意到瓶颈、空白、那些没人构建过的开发工具，其中之一可能会成为实际的公司。

speaker: Unknown
en: Here's what I want you to take away from this video.
zh: 这就是我希望你从这个视频中带走的内容。

speaker: Unknown
en: First, stop trying to find the perfect idea.
zh: 首先，停止试图寻找完美的想法。

speaker: Unknown
en: Just pick one.
zh: 就选一个。

speaker: Unknown
en: Then burn the other boats.
zh: 然后烧掉其他的船。

speaker: Unknown
en: Learn everything you can about the customer and try to execute for them.
zh: 尽你所能了解关于客户的一切，并尝试为他们执行。

speaker: Unknown
en: In the early idea fog, where you can only see 10 feet in front of you, the temptation is to take a few cautious steps in every direction.
zh: 在早期的想法迷雾中，你只能看清前方 10 英尺，这种诱惑是向每个方向试探性地走几步。

speaker: Unknown
en: Sample a little here, a little there, stay close to home.
zh: 在这里采样一点，在那里采样一点，呆在家里。

speaker: Unknown
en: The problem is that gives you almost no information.
zh: 问题是那几乎没给你任何信息。

speaker: Unknown
en: What actually works is to commit to one direction and walk fast.
zh: 真正有效的是致力于一个方向并快速行走。

speaker: Unknown
en: You're not guaranteed to end up in the right place, but you generate much more information per unit of time.
zh: 你不保证最终会到达正确的地方，但你在单位时间内产生更多的信息。

speaker: Unknown
en: And when you're walking, you might arrive at a better destination.
zh: 而当你行走时，你可能会到达一个更好的目的地。

speaker: Unknown
en: One you couldn't have seen from the start.
zh: 一个你从一开始就无法看到的（目的地）。

speaker: Unknown
en: The worst failure mode isn't being wrong.
zh: 最糟糕的失败模式不是犯错。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's not making a decision, spinning your wheels, dabbling between ideas and never going deep enough on any one of them to learn anything.
zh: 它是不做决定、空转、在想法之间涉猎，并且从未在任何一个上深入到足以学到任何东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: So pick one and go deep.
zh: 所以选一个并深入去做。

speaker: Unknown
en: Thanks for watching.
zh: 谢谢观看。
